text:
Jared Spencer (Food Scientist - SharkNinja | Founder of RIDDIM Snacks)
Spent the day at Tooting Works mentoring their Business Launchpad cohort on all things business, specifically, the power of storytelling as a startup. 

​Didnt claim to have all the answers, but we dove deep into how RIDDIM Snacks is leveraging Caribbean Culture to drive commercial viability, incrementality and mass appeal.

From Scotch Bonnet Chilli Jam to Customised Dual Heritage Flags the truth is, there has never been a lack of innovation within our community; there’s a lack of opportunity. 

So massive shoutout to Nicole Margarita Henworth Polina Changuleva and the whole Tooting Works team for creating a space where young people can genuinely create, iterate, and execute their ideas. RIDDIM will always back you guys.

Job Well Done! Adama Sesay  Tianna-Monique Ince- Sam Ikhuoria RepYourFlags

Deirdre Taylor (Consultant Home Economist/Consumer Appliance Expert — Freelance — Gerrards Cross, United Kingdom)
well done Jared, you are a great mentor

Scotch bonnet & chedduh went down a treat!

Fanstastic, Sam! - have you been in touch with Lucy Neal, our Environment Guest tutor, who is working in Tooting - I think it would be a good connection -

Amazing Jared👏🏽

OBI CHINONSO DAVID (🚀 Founder @ Nosyra Digital | Systems • Scaling • Business Growth — Freelance — Lagos, Nigeria)
This is the kind of mentorship that actually moves communities forward. You didn't just share theory  you showed how RIDDIM Snacks leverages culture as a commercial strategy, turning Scotch Bonnet Chilli Jam and dual heritage pride into mass appeal. That insight about 'innovation isn't lacking, opportunity is that's the real talk young founders need to hear. Spaces like Tooting Works where people can create, iterate, and execute without gatekeeping are rare. Thank you for showing up, sharing your journey authentically, and helping the next generation see that their culture isn't just heritage  it's a competitive advantage.
